text: hm.... will you put in a fps reader on the compiled game path so i can track it better
resolution: Added an on-screen fps HUD to the compiled game path (RJIT_FPS=1 or RJIT_PERFLOG=1): a top-left readout of fps / draw(us) / inst / restage / dc, so the user can track fps on-screen instead of terminal logs. fps is wall-clock frame-to-frame (so it reflects GPU overdraw stalls and the SDL 60fps cap, unlike the CPU-only draw_us), and 'restage' is the per-frame re-uploaded instance count — together they let the user see at a glance whether a slow view is a CPU re-stage choke or GPU overdraw. Implemented entirely in framework/gpu/3d.zig (clean file, no world_loader.zig edit). Key correctness fix: the HUD text is queued from scene3d.render() (the paint walk, before gpu.frame), NOT from flushPending — gpu.frame uploads the text buffer BEFORE calling flushPending, so glyphs queued in flushPending upload too late and never draw (first attempt showed a blank HUD; moving to render() fixed it). Verified the HUD renders via rjit game shot (text visible top-left). Self-gated, zero behavior change when the env vars are unset.
